subject.title: feat(durable): add beta3 runtime core foundation

question: Which durable-runtime stack, if any, should become the canonical core landing path, and should it use one lifecycle-owned shared-state repository?
rationale: Multiple overlapping implementations exist, and this PR creates permanent runtime, persistence, protocol, CLI, configuration, and operator-policy contracts that code review cannot accept without maintainer product and architecture ownership.

options.title: Sponsor this narrowed rebuilt stack
options.body: Choose this stack as canonical, integrate storage into the shared-state owner, reduce controls, prove it live, and then close superseded earlier PRs.

options.title: Continue an earlier stack
options.body: Keep the strongest prior implementation as canonical and preserve any unique fixes from this rebuilt branch before closing it.

options.title: Pause durable core
options.body: Do not select a landing path until the core product need and long-term persistence boundary are narrower.

recommendation.title: Sponsor this narrowed rebuilt stack
recommendation.body: Choose this stack as canonical, integrate storage into the shared-state owner, reduce controls, prove it live, and then close superseded earlier PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged history shows the strongest ownership signal across the shared-state, gateway, and agent surfaces, and this decision spans core product architecture.
